---
title: "Contacts across physical levels"
description: "Model intended connections and clearances in bumps, posts, decks and excitation supports."
sidebar: simulation
---

A contact declaration must correspond to the modeled conductor connection.
A non-contact crossing must retain its clearance. The final product must make
both inspectable before its matrices or fields are interpreted.

## Input supplied by OrPen

- Positive metal regions/holes and intended body-to-body contacts.
- Physical levels, material, finite Z and opposing face orientation.
- Same-Net membership, separate Nets and intended crossing clearances.
- Named nonmetal supports, contact conductors, normals and directed integration/current lines.

A support rectangle is not conductor metal. A Ground label alone is not
evidence that two bodies touch.

## Backend requirements

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Palace

| Stage | Required delivery |
| --- | --- |
| Native geometry | Preserve requested conductor interfaces and PEC exclusions; identify shared boundaries and dielectric/air gaps. |
| Electrical assignment | Preserve potential/PEC/lumped selections and intended Net meaning. |
| Discretization | Show the shared-interface mesh topology for requested conformal contacts; do not replace intended contact with coincident disconnected faces. |
| Results | Keep current/field/energy or capacitance interpretation bound to the modeled contacts. |

### AEDT

| Stage | Required delivery |
| --- | --- |
| Native geometry | Build contacting bodies/sheets and actual gaps under the selected Z map; expose overlap and endpoint placement. |
| Electrical assignment | Preserve one-Net/multiple-body membership and exact port/terminal reference targets. |
| Discretization | Let native meshing use the declared model; retain geometry/assignment readback separately from adaptive evidence. |
| Results | Keep matrix/terminal/field output bound to actual native body and Net assignments. |

:::

Grouping must retain source ownership and holes without creating unintended
shorts. One Net may contain several native bodies; their shared label does
not replace observation of the intended interfaces.

## Final product to inspect

- Flip-chip: bump endpoints on lower and upper Ground; central Pad remains separate.
- Airbridge: deck-to-post and post-to-Ground contacts; bridge crosses Signal without touching it.
- Lumped support: native support plane, terminal owners and current direction.
- A native geometry/contact view followed by the relevant mesh/assignment and solved-output evidence.

Use the [small bump and airbridge coupons](../../public-pdk-examples/test-components.md)
for these contact questions; the larger resonator serves the system-level port
question. No new numerical contact tolerance is specified.

::: {.callout-note title="Follow each intended interface"}

[Multilevel contacts](../../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/GeometrySemantics/geometry_multilevel_contacts.ipynb)
shows the bump/lower-Ground and bump/upper-Ground interfaces, and the
deck/post/base-Ground chain. Inspect source footprints and Z first, actual
native contact/clearance next, and mesh or terminal assignment before reading
the corresponding solved quantity. Signal clearance is a separate required
observation from Ground continuity.

:::

For lumped excitation, retain the support's normal separately from its
directed Signal-to-Ground current/integration line. A correct support plane
does not by itself establish the terminal owners or direction.

Serves [capacitance](../requirements/electrostatic-capacitance.qmd),
[lumped RLC](../requirements/lumped-rlc-eigenmode.qmd),
[driven terminal](../requirements/driven-terminal.qmd) and [Q3D](../requirements/q3d-acrl.qmd).
